terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Build the pickup shelf here and run it, after you call your functions from main. Ctrl+C stops a program that waits for typing.

tasks.title: Look for a name on the shelf
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1` in `src/shelf.cpp`, write a function called `onShelf` that takes the shelf as a reference to a `const std::vector<std::string>` and a name as a reference to a `const std::string`. It gives back `true` when that name is on the shelf, written exactly the same, and `false` when it is not.

Check calls `onShelf` from code of its own with shelves of its own, an empty one included, and names that are first, last or not there. It only reads the shelf, so the caller's shelf must be the same afterwards.
nextSteps: Write the first line: two `const` references in, a `bool` back.
Go through the shelf and compare each name with the one asked for.
Decide where `false` can be given back: only once every name has been looked at.
Call it from `main` with a name on the shelf and one that is not.
hints: The answer is only `false` once the whole shelf has been looked at, so that `return` comes after the loop.
Inside the loop, `return true;` as soon as a name matches. An `else` that gives back `false` inside the loop stops after the first name.
The shape is `for (const auto& customer : shelf) { if (customer == name) { return true; } } return false;`.

tasks.title: Put the new arrivals on the shelf
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 2`, write a function called `shelveAll` that takes the shelf as a reference to a `std::vector<std::string>` and the names that arrived as a reference to a `const std::vector<std::string>`, and gives nothing back. It adds every name that arrived to the end of the caller's shelf, in the order they arrived. The names that arrived stay as they were.

Check calls `shelveAll` with a shelf and arrivals of its own, empty ones included, and reads both after the call: the shelf must have changed, and the arrivals must not have.
nextSteps: Write the first line: which list changes, and which is only read?
Go through the names that arrived.
Add each one to the end of the shelf.
In `main`, shelve a few names and print the shelf's size afterwards.
hints: The shelf changes for the caller, so it is a reference without `const`. The arrivals are only read, so they are a `const` reference.
`push_back` adds one name at the end. Going through the arrivals in order keeps their order.
The shape is `void shelveAll(std::vector<std::string>& shelf, const std::vector<std::string>& arrived) { for (const auto& name : arrived) { shelf.push_back(name); } }`.

tasks.title: List the names that start with a letter
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3`, write a function called `startingWith` that takes the shelf as a reference to a `const std::vector<std::string>` and a letter as a `char`. It gives back a new `std::vector<std::string>` with the names on the shelf whose first character is that letter, in shelf order, and leaves the shelf as it was. With the shelf below and `'O'`, it gives back `{"Oona Pruett", "Odran Selby"}`:

```
{"Oona Pruett", "Mirelle Vantry", "Odran Selby"}
```

Check calls `startingWith` with shelves and letters of its own, a letter no name starts with and an empty shelf included, and reads what it gives back and the caller's shelf afterwards. It prints nothing.
nextSteps: Write the first line, with a new vector as what it gives back.
Make an empty vector of names inside the function.
Go through the shelf, and add each name whose first character is the letter.
Give the new vector back, and print what it holds in `main`.
hints: The caller's shelf stays as it was, so the names found go into a new vector the function makes itself.
A text's first character is at position 0, as in the text issue. Compare it with the letter, and `push_back` the name into the new vector when they match.
The shape is `std::vector<std::string> found; for (const auto& name : shelf) { if (!name.empty() && name[0] == letter) { found.push_back(name); } } return found;`.

tasks.title: Read the ticket numbers Dorrit types
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 4`, write a function called `readTickets` that takes nothing. It reads whole numbers from `std::cin`, one after another, until Dorrit types `0`, and gives back a `std::vector<int>` with every number she typed before the `0`, in order. The `0` only means she is done; it is not a ticket.

Check calls `readTickets` and types numbers of its own on its standard input, some on one line and some on several, with the `0` at the end, and reads what it gives back. A function that reads on after the `0` would sit and wait in the terminal; Check notices that and says so.
nextSteps: Write the first line: nothing in, a `std::vector<int>` back.
Make an empty vector and an `int` to read into.
Write a loop that reads a number and goes on while it is not 0.
Add each number to the vector, give it back, and try it by typing in the terminal.
hints: A read with `>>` can stand in a condition, like in the reading-input issue: true when it worked.
`std::cin >> ticket && ticket != 0` reads first and then asks about the number. As a `while` condition, the loop stops at the 0 without adding it.
The shape is `std::vector<int> tickets; int ticket = 0; while (std::cin >> ticket && ticket != 0) { tickets.push_back(ticket); } return tickets;`.
